full_judgment:
Khademul Islam Chowdhury J: This Rule at the instance of accused-petitioner Sree Rani Krishna Nath (Ram Babu) was issued under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceedings of GR Case No. 393 of 2005 corresponding to Kotwali Police Station Case No. 16(6) 2005, now pending before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong should not be quashed. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that on 12-8-2004 JCO 3432 Subedar Md Harun Miah, of 43 Rifle Battalion, Halishahar as informant lodged first information report with Kotwali Police Station alleging that on 11-8-2004 on receipt of secret information of massive accumulation of local currency at the shop called "Nath Jewellers" at Khatunganj Boxirhat, Chittagong the informant accompanied by joint force on search into shop room, recovered huge amount of local currency in the iron safe vault along with gold and silver ornaments contained in three hundred and fifty plastic bags, having gold ornaments stored in one hundred in each plastic bag paper packets. It is alleged that the nature of storage and location indicate that the proprietor of the jewellery shop illegally brought golden biscuit and bar and by transforming those into ornaments in no time with the help of his employees carried on unlawful trade. Thereafter, all the rooms opened by the informant were sealed and left in the jimma of one Mr Mohammad Hossain, Secretary of Banik Kalyan Samity, Khatunganj; The owner was given time under the advice of the task force who failed to produce any record in support of the business and no one on behalf of the concerned proprietor of Nath Jewellers turned up. 

 3. On receipt of first information report on 12-8-2004 at 20-10 hours Kotwali PS Case No. 24 dated 12-8-2004 under section 25B of the Special Powers Act, 1974 was started against 8(eight) accused-persons including the accused-petitioner arid first information report named accuseds 2-7 were arrested. The informant deposited seized alamats namely, gold and silver ornaments, cash money and stones, with Bangladesh Bank, Chittagong. Accused-petitioner Sree Ram Krishna Nath surrendered and obtained bail from the High Court Division and submitted application for return of the seized gold ornaments with cash money and other materials recovered from his shop. Subsequently, 46(forty-six) persons as claimants also submitted applications for return of seized ornaments. 

 5. On sending the record of the case to the Metropolitan Special Court No.1, it was registered as Special Tribunal Case No. 108 of 2008. On 15-5-2005 an application for return of the seized mate rials and cash money along with the Registers was filed before the Tribunal on behalf of the accused petitioner. 

 6. The learned Judge of the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No, 1 after hearing both the parties accepted the Final Report, discharged the accused persons from the case by order dated 15-5-2005 with the direction for return of seized materials and the money to the accused-petitioner Ram Krishna Nath alias Ram Babu, The Tribunal further directed the accused-petitioner on getting delivery of the seized materials from the Court to return to other claimants who deposited gold ornaments with him, as per seized Register and report compliance to the Tribunal within 1( one) month. The Tribunal further directed the concerned custodians to return the seized ornaments and cash money to the accused petitioner and communicate the copy of the order to the Officer-in-Charge Kotwali Police Station, CMP and Manager Bangladesh Bank for compliance. 

 7. Thereafter, on 7-6-2005 informant Subeder Md Harun Mia submitted petition for further investigation before the Tribunal below alleging, inter alia, that business of the accused petitioner involved crores of Taka and huge cash money was recovered form the secret vault not supported by any bank record might be used for hundi business. The informant also filed second first information report over the self-same occurrence on the same date (7-6-2005) but this time against the accused-petitioner as the sole accused. It is alleged that the informant by conducting raid with the help of District Task Force recovered seized gold and money from Nath Jewellers. On the basis of his written first information report earlier case No. 24(8)04 under section 25B(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 was initiated. Since no valid papers were available in support of huge cash money he filed the fresh case against the accused-petitioner on which Kotwali PS Case No. 16(6)05 was started. 

 8. Thereafter, on 9-6-2005 the investigation officer in the second first information report filed an application praying for showing the seized alamat of Kotwali PS Case No. 24(8)04 as the seized alamat in the said Case No. 16(6)05 and, in the meanwhile, safe custody of the alamats to continue till disposal of the case which was allowed by the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 9. The learned Special Tribunal No.1, Chittagong after hearing both the parties rejected the prayer for further investigation by order dated 13-6-2005 on finding that earlier Case No. 24(8)04 was finally decided on acceptance of the final report after hearing both the parties with the consent of the public prosecutor and so the Tribunal ceased to have jurisdiction to pass any order for further investigation; Consequently, the cash money found in the vault of the shop "Nath Jewellers" is not the account of business transaction as mentioned in the final report prevailed. 

 10. Thereafter, police on completion of investigation submitted charge sheet on 30-9-2005 in the case arising out of the second first information report. 

 11. Being aggrieved by the impugned proceeding of GR Case No. 393 of 2005 corresponding to Kotwali PS Case No. 16(6) 2005 under section 13 of the Money Laundering Pratirode Ain, 2002 the accused-petitioner moved this court and obtained the Rule. 

 12. Mr Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner with Mr AKM Faiz and HS Deb Brahman, submits that the facts disclosed in both the cases (24-8-2004 and 16-6-2005) arising out of same occurrence, on face value, do not constitute any offence of Money laundering Pratirode Ain, 2002 and, as such, initiation of the case and further continuance of the proceeding is out and out baseless, frivolous, fictitious, malicious and vindictive which is calculated to destroy the business of the accused petitioner and to harass and victimise the accused petitioner, is wholly unwarranted, as such, abuse of the process of the court and liable to be quashed. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the final and conclusive finding and decision of the Special Tribunal No.1 in Special Tribunal Case No. 108 of2008 that the cash money recovered from the shop is on account of daily transactions and the direction of the learned Tribunal dated 15-5-2005 for return of the gold and silver ornaments and the cash money to the accused-petitioner, the second first information report lodged by the informant on baseless and frivolous allegation that cash money recovered is not accounted for or it is intended to be used for hundi business, is prima facie frivolous and baseless and the same constitutes no criminal offence and further prolongation of the case is calculated to cause harassment to an innocent party and, as such, the proceeding is liable to be quashed. 

 13. The learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State, submits that allegations as made in the first information report Case No. 16(6)05 constitute an offence of money laundering as alleged and, as such, the proceeding cannot be quashed at this stage. 

 14. We have perused the first information report, Final Report in Case No. 24(8) 2007, Charge Sheet and the Annexure on record carefully and the relevant provisions of law. 

 15. Now, even if the allegations made in the 2nd first information report are taken to be true that local currency of huge amount has been recovered from the safe vault of Nath Jewellers an on-going business of money lending on mortgage of gold ornament, making of and sale and purchase of ornaments not accounted for by any bank paper and money might be brought for hundi business, the same, in our view, do not constitute any offence under section 25B of the Special Powers Act or under section 13 of the Money Laundering Act, 2002 or under any law of the land. If any Bangladeshi National is found in possession of Bangladesh currency notes of any amount, he cannot be taken to have committed any offence under the law of the land and the proceedings at the stage of first information report can be quashed to secure ends of justice. In this connection, the case of Abdul Quader vs State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38 is the case on the point wherein it has observed as under: 

 "Case may also arise where the allegations in the first information report or the complaint even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence alleged. In such cases, no question of appreciating evidence arises, it is a matter of looking at the complaint, or the first information report to decide whether the offence alleged is disclosed or not. In such cases it would be legitimate for the High Court to hold that it would be manifestly unjust to allow process of the Criminal Court to be issued against the accused persons. 

 16. In another unreported case of Tozammel Hoque and another vide Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6609 of 2003 the High Court Division has held- 

 If such possession is taken to have constituted any criminal offence it would also be a clear case of violation of the fundamental rights of free movement or carrying on trade or business by a citizen of Bangladesh as guaranteed under Articles 36 and 40 of the Constitution. 

 17. Moreso, it is revealed in the investigation of the first case (Kotwali PS Case No. 24(8)2004 arising out of the same occurrence, that money recovered from the vault of the iron safe of Nath Jewellers is on account of daily transaction. 

 18. The Special Tribunal No.1, Chittagong, accepted the Final Report and discharged the accused petitioner with direction upon the concerned authorities to return the seized articles including the money to the accused petitioner as aforesaid. After rejection of the prayer for further investigation by the Tribunal, the charge sheet is then submitted by the police in the second case accusing the accused petitioner on the self-same occurrence is malicious, calculated to victimise and harass the accused petitioner and further proceeding in the case will be an abuse of the process of the Court. 

 20. The proceeding of Kotwali Police Station Case No. 16(6)05, now pending before the Special Tribunal No. 1, Chittagong, is hereby quashed. 

 21. The informant is directed to return the original receipts of safe deposit of the seized articles and the money deposited with Bangladesh Bank to the accused petitioner of the case. The Commander of 43 Rifle Battalion, Halishahar, Chittagong, as the recipient of original receipt of Bangladesh Bank in respect of seized articles, is directed to ensure return of original Safe Deposit Annexure-C1-C4 to the Joint Manager, Banking (Bangladesh Bank), Chittagong Branch, opposite party No.2 herein.
